editorial:
You follow Detective Ma Seok-do as he leaves his old station for the Metropolitan Investigation Team, chasing Japanese gangsters who crossed into Korea to run violent crimes. The vibe is pure popcorn action with big punches, quick jokes, and a no-nonsense hero who solves problems with his fists and a grin. If you loved the earlier Roundup films, you know the rhythm: Ma walks in, bad guys panic, and the screen fills with bone-crunching fights. This time the stakes feel bigger because the villains are organized, ruthless, and willing to hurt anyone in their way. The story moves fast, jumping between police work and street brawls, so you never sit still for long.

The standout is Ma Dong-seok, whose charm and physical presence carry every scene. The action is loud and fun, and the humor lands well. On the downside, the plot feels familiar if you have seen the previous entries, and some side characters do not get much to do. Still, if you want a crowd-pleasing action movie with heart and humor, this delivers. It is perfect for a weekend movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final act, Ma Seok-do tracks the Japanese gang leader to a showdown after uncovering the drug ring behind the murders. The twist is that a trusted ally's connection to the gang is exposed, forcing Ma to fight through waves of henchmen alone. After a brutal final brawl, Ma takes down the boss and saves the hostages. The movie ends with Ma back on duty, joking with his team, hinting that more trouble is always around the corner.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action-packed crime thrillers with humor and heart.
